quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Sam joined a painting class on Saturday mornings. He learned how to mix colours and create shading. By the end of the month he had completed three paintings.
options: Sam joined a Saturday morning painting class.
He learned to mix colours and create shading.
Sam had completed three paintings by month's end.
Sam gave up after his first class.
quests.hint: Follow the learning story: joining, learning skills, then the result. One frame contradicts the progress shown.
quests.explanation: Learning narratives show enrolment, skill development, and an achievement. The distractor replaces progress with quitting.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The friends planned a trip to the cinema for Friday evening. They booked tickets online in advance. They met outside the cinema and went in together.
options: The friends watched the film at home instead.
The friends planned a Friday evening cinema trip.
They booked their tickets online in advance.
They met outside the cinema and went in together.
quests.hint: Trace the cinema trip: planning, booking, then going together. One frame replaces the outing with a stay-at-home alternative.
quests.explanation: Social outing narratives follow plan, book, and attend. The distractor replaces the outing with a home-based activity.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The hiking group set off early in the morning. They followed the trail through the forest for three hours. They reached the summit and admired the view.
options: The hiking group set off early in the morning.
They followed the forest trail for three hours.
The group turned back halfway due to bad weather.
They reached the summit and admired the view.
quests.hint: Follow the hike: setting off, the trail, then reaching the top. One frame stops the journey halfway.
quests.explanation: Journey narratives show departure, travel, and arrival at the destination. The distractor cuts the journey short.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Amy decided to redecorate her bedroom. She chose a soft blue paint and bought new curtains. The bedroom looked fresh and bright after the makeover.
options: Amy decided to redecorate her bedroom.
Amy's parents refused to let her change the room.
She chose blue paint and bought new curtains.
The bedroom looked fresh and bright afterwards.
quests.hint: Sequence the makeover: deciding, choosing materials, then the result. One frame blocks the project entirely.
quests.explanation: Home improvement narratives show decision, action, and a pleasing result. The distractor introduces a parental veto not in the story.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The local football team won their first match of the season. The manager praised the team's hard work and dedication. The whole town celebrated with a parade.
options: The local football team won their first match.
The manager praised the team's hard work.
The whole town celebrated with a parade.
The football team lost and the season ended early.
quests.hint: Follow the victory story: winning, being praised, then the town celebration. One frame reverses the outcome.
quests.explanation: Celebration narratives show success, recognition, and community joy. The distractor replaces all three with failure.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Josh found his grandfather's old guitar in the attic. He took it to a music shop to have it tuned and repaired. He then taught himself three chords from a video online.
options: Josh sold the guitar immediately for money.
Josh found his grandfather's old guitar in the attic.
He took it to a music shop to be tuned and repaired.
Josh taught himself three chords from an online video.
quests.hint: Trace the musical journey: finding, restoring, then learning to play. One frame skips the learning entirely.
quests.explanation: Discovery and learning narratives show finding, restoring, and acquiring a skill. The distractor replaces learning with selling.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The school announced a fundraising bake sale. Students spent the weekend baking cakes, biscuits, and muffins. The sale raised over three hundred pounds for charity.
options: The school announced a fundraising bake sale.
Students baked cakes, biscuits, and muffins at the weekend.
The school cancelled the bake sale at the last minute.
The sale raised over three hundred pounds for charity.
quests.hint: Follow the fundraising story: announcement, preparation, then the result. One frame cancels the event before it starts.
quests.explanation: Fundraising narratives show announcement, preparation, and a successful outcome. The distractor removes the event entirely.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The twins wanted to surprise their father for his birthday. They made a card and baked his favourite chocolate cake. When he came home, they shouted surprise.
options: The twins wanted to surprise their father for his birthday.
Their father found out about the surprise in advance.
They made a card and baked his favourite chocolate cake.
They shouted surprise when he came home.
quests.hint: Sequence the surprise: planning, preparing, then revealing. One frame ruins the surprise before the climax.
quests.explanation: Surprise narratives build tension through planning and preparation, then release with the reveal. The distractor removes the tension by revealing the plan early.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The community centre advertised a free yoga class. Many residents signed up and arrived with their mats. The instructor led them through a relaxing one-hour session.
options: The community centre advertised a free yoga class.
Many residents signed up and arrived with their mats.
The instructor led a relaxing one-hour session.
Nobody signed up for the yoga class.
quests.hint: Follow the yoga story: advertising, residents signing up, then the class itself. One frame shows no interest.
quests.explanation: Community activity narratives show advertising, participation, and delivery. The distractor replaces community engagement with no interest.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: It was the first day of the new school term. Students found their new classrooms and met their teachers. By the end of the day they were already making new friends.
options: Most students refused to go into school on the first day.
It was the first day of the new school term.
Students found their classrooms and met their teachers.
By day's end students were already making new friends.
quests.hint: Trace the first day: arriving, settling in, then connecting socially. One frame contradicts the positive settling-in.
quests.explanation: First-day narratives show arrival, orientation, and social connection. The distractor introduces refusal that contradicts the positive experience.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The science experiment required vinegar and bicarbonate of soda. The students carefully measured and mixed the two substances. The mixture fizzed and bubbled dramatically.
options: The science experiment required vinegar and bicarbonate of soda.
Students carefully measured and mixed the substances.
The experiment produced no reaction at all.
The mixture fizzed and bubbled dramatically.
quests.hint: Follow the experiment: gathering materials, mixing, then the result. One frame gives the wrong chemical outcome.
quests.explanation: Experiment narratives show preparation, process, and result. The distractor replaces a dramatic reaction with no result.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Lena received a scholarship to study art abroad. She packed her suitcase and said goodbye to her family. She arrived at the art school full of excitement.
options: Lena received a scholarship to study art abroad.
Lena turned down the scholarship and stayed home.
She packed her suitcase and said goodbye to her family.
She arrived at the art school full of excitement.
quests.hint: Sequence the scholarship story: receiving, packing and farewell, then arriving. One frame refuses the opportunity.
quests.explanation: Scholarship narratives show success, preparation, and a new beginning. The distractor replaces acceptance with refusal.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The restaurant was fully booked for Valentine's Day. Dan called three days early to reserve a table. He arrived with flowers and surprised his partner.
options: The restaurant was fully booked for Valentine's Day.
Dan called three days early to reserve a table.
He arrived with flowers and surprised his partner.
Dan forgot to make a reservation and they could not get in.
quests.hint: Follow the planning story: full bookings, planning ahead, then the successful evening. One frame shows failure to plan.
quests.explanation: Romantic planning narratives show foresight, reservation, and a successful occasion. The distractor replaces planning with forgetting.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The youth club collected donations of old clothes. They sorted and washed the clothes at the community hall. The items were given to a local charity shop.
options: The youth club threw away all the old clothes.
The youth club collected old clothes as donations.
They sorted and washed the clothes at the hall.
The clothes were given to a local charity shop.
quests.hint: Trace the donation drive: collecting, sorting, then donating. One frame replaces a charitable act with waste.
quests.explanation: Community service narratives show collecting, preparing, and donating. The distractor replaces donation with disposal.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The town library held a reading week for children. Children visited every day to collect stamps in their reading passports. The top readers won gift vouchers at the end.
options: The library held a reading week for children.
Children visited daily to collect stamps in their passports.
Very few children took part in the reading week.
Top readers won gift vouchers at the end.
quests.hint: Sequence the event: the reading week, daily participation, then the reward. One frame shows poor participation.
quests.explanation: Incentive narratives show an event, active participation, and a reward. The distractor replaces strong participation with low engagement.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The weather forecast predicted a heatwave for the coming week. Schools sent letters home advising students to bring water bottles. Students arrived each day well prepared.
options: A heatwave was forecast for the coming week.
Students arrived without water and were sent home.
Schools advised students to bring water bottles.
Students arrived each day well prepared.
quests.hint: Follow the preparation story: the forecast, the school advice, then students being prepared. One frame shows unpreparedness.
quests.explanation: Preparation narratives show warning, advice, and readiness. The distractor replaces readiness with failure to prepare.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The young designer entered her first fashion competition. She worked for weeks designing and sewing her outfit. She won second place and was invited to show her work at a showcase.
options: The designer entered her first fashion competition.
She designed and sewed her outfit over several weeks.
She won second place and was invited to a showcase.
The designer lost confidence and withdrew from the competition.
quests.hint: Trace the competition: entering, creating the outfit, then the result. One frame removes the achievement.
quests.explanation: Competition narratives show entering, preparing, and achieving recognition. The distractor replaces an achievement with withdrawal.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: A local journalist investigated reports of noise pollution from a nearby factory. She spoke with residents and gathered evidence. Her article led to an official environmental review.
options: The journalist decided not to publish the story.
A journalist investigated reports of noise pollution.
She spoke with residents and gathered evidence.
Her article led to an official environmental review.
quests.hint: Sequence the journalism story: investigating, gathering evidence, then publishing with impact. One frame removes the outcome.
quests.explanation: Investigative narratives show research, evidence gathering, and impactful publication. The distractor removes the act of publishing.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The new teacher introduced a reading competition in the first week. Students were encouraged to read as many books as they could each month. The winners were announced at assembly.
options: The teacher introduced a reading competition in the first week.
Students were encouraged to read as many books as possible.
The competition was never officially announced to students.
Winners were announced at the school assembly.
quests.hint: Follow the initiative: introduction, participation, then the announcement. One frame removes the original announcement.
quests.explanation: Competition narratives show introduction, engagement, and recognition. The distractor creates a contradiction by removing the announcement.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The rescue team searched the mountain for a missing hiker. They found footprints in the snow leading to a shelter. The hiker was discovered safe inside.
options: The rescue team searched the mountain for a missing hiker.
The rescue team abandoned the search due to bad weather.
They found footprints in the snow leading to a shelter.
The hiker was found safe inside the shelter.
quests.hint: Trace the rescue: searching, finding a clue, then discovering the hiker. One frame stops the rescue mid-search.
quests.explanation: Rescue narratives follow search, discovery of a clue, and resolution. The distractor replaces resolution with abandonment.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The photography club organised an outdoor shoot in the city. Members explored different streets and captured interesting buildings. Their best photos were displayed in the school hall.
options: The photography club organised an outdoor city shoot.
Members explored streets and photographed buildings.
Their best photos were displayed in the school hall.
The club's photographs were all deleted accidentally.
quests.hint: Follow the photography story: organising, capturing images, then displaying them. One frame removes the display with accidental deletion.
quests.explanation: Creative project narratives show organising, creating, and displaying work. The distractor replaces display with accidental loss.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The students prepared a presentation for their science project. They used charts, diagrams, and a short video to explain their findings. Their teacher gave them the highest marks in the class.
options: The students forgot to prepare slides for the presentation.
Students prepared a presentation for their science project.
They used charts, diagrams, and a video to explain findings.
Their teacher gave them the highest marks in the class.
quests.hint: Sequence the project: preparation, presenting with visuals, then the result. One frame contradicts the preparation shown.
quests.explanation: Academic presentation narratives show preparation, delivery, and reward. The distractor contradicts the careful preparation described.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Maya signed up to volunteer at the local food bank. She sorted donated tins and packaged food parcels each Saturday. The food bank manager thanked her for her dedication.
options: Maya signed up to volunteer at the local food bank.
She sorted tins and packaged food parcels each Saturday.
Maya only volunteered once and never went back.
The food bank manager thanked her for her dedication.
quests.hint: Follow the volunteer story: signing up, consistent work, then recognition. One frame contradicts the dedication with a single visit.
quests.explanation: Volunteer narratives show commitment, consistent effort, and appreciation. The distractor replaces consistency with a single visit.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The family went on a road trip for the bank holiday weekend. They drove through three counties, stopping at villages and viewpoints along the way. They returned home tired but happy.
options: The family went on a road trip for the bank holiday.
The family's car broke down and they returned early.
They drove through three counties, stopping along the way.
They returned home tired but happy.
quests.hint: Trace the road trip: setting out, exploring, then arriving home happy. One frame ends the trip prematurely.
quests.explanation: Road trip narratives show departure, exploration, and a happy return. The distractor introduces a breakdown that ends the trip early.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The artist began a new mural on the side of a town building. He sketched the outline first in chalk, then began applying layers of paint. After two weeks of work, the finished mural was unveiled.
options: The artist began a new mural on a town building.
He sketched the outline in chalk before painting.
The finished mural was unveiled after two weeks.
Residents complained and the mural was painted over.
quests.hint: Follow the creation story: starting, the process, then unveiling. One frame destroys the finished work.
quests.explanation: Artistic creation narratives show beginning, process, and completion. The distractor introduces community opposition that was not in the story.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The drama class rehearsed their play every day after school. They memorised their lines and practised their movements on stage. On the night of the performance, they received a standing ovation.
options: Half the cast forgot their lines during the performance.
The drama class rehearsed their play every day.
They memorised lines and practised movements on stage.
They received a standing ovation on performance night.
quests.hint: Trace the performance story: daily rehearsal, learning and practising, then the response. One frame contradicts the dedicated preparation.
quests.explanation: Performance narratives show rehearsal, mastery, and audience acclaim. The distractor replaces a standing ovation with a forgotten-lines disaster.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: A group of school friends entered a local quiz competition. They studied different topics each evening for a month. They came in first place and won a hundred-pound prize.
options: School friends entered a local quiz competition.
They studied different topics each evening for a month.
The friends lost in the first round of the quiz.
They came first and won a hundred-pound prize.
quests.hint: Sequence the competition: entering, preparing consistently, then the result. One frame replaces winning with early elimination.
quests.explanation: Quiz competition narratives show entry, dedicated preparation, and a winning outcome. The distractor replaces the win with early elimination.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The local community garden was overgrown and neglected. Volunteers arrived on a Saturday morning with tools and gloves. By afternoon the garden was cleared, planted, and looking beautiful.
options: The community garden was overgrown and neglected.
The council decided to build a car park on the garden.
Volunteers arrived with tools and gloves on Saturday.
By afternoon the garden was cleared and looking beautiful.
quests.hint: Follow the garden story: the problem, volunteers arriving, then the transformation. One frame removes the garden entirely.
quests.explanation: Community restoration narratives show a problem, volunteer action, and a beautiful result. The distractor replaces restoration with demolition.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The explorer set off on an expedition through the Amazon jungle. She navigated rivers and dense forest for six weeks. She returned with new plant and insect specimens for scientific study.
options: The explorer set off on an Amazon expedition.
She navigated rivers and dense forest for six weeks.
She returned with new plant and insect specimens.
The expedition ended after just two days due to illness.
quests.hint: Trace the expedition: departing, navigating the jungle, then returning with discoveries. One frame ends the trip early.
quests.explanation: Expedition narratives show departure, journey, and discovery. The distractor cuts the journey short before discoveries are made.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The new hospital wing was officially opened by the mayor. Nurses, doctors, and staff lined the corridors to welcome the first patients. The first patient walked in just after ten o'clock.
options: The hospital wing was delayed and stayed closed.
The mayor officially opened the new hospital wing.
Staff lined the corridors to welcome the first patients.
The first patient walked in just after ten o'clock.
quests.hint: Sequence the opening: the ceremony, staff welcoming, then the first arrival. One frame delays the opening indefinitely.
quests.explanation: Official opening narratives show the ceremony, a welcoming atmosphere, and the first use of the new facility. The distractor postpones the opening.
